outcomes.goal: Give a destination with į and an appropriate noun form.

models.title: Going to a place
pairs: I am going to the bank.
I am going to the park.
models.note: Einu means I am going on foot. After į (to), bankas becomes banką and parkas becomes parką. Keep the action the same; change the destination.

models.title: Same action, different endings
pairs: I am going to the café.
I am going to the museum.
models.note: After į, kavinė becomes kavinę (-ė → -ę), and muziejus becomes muziejų (-us → -ų). The destination rule stays the same.

checks.translation: We are going to the bank.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: A destination after į takes banką.

checks.translation: We are going to the café.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: A destination after į uses kavinę.

checks.translation: On Friday I am going to the station.
checks.hint: Check the person, time or preposition beside the gap.
checks.correction: After į: stotį.

checks.translation: Rasa is going to the museum.
checks.hint: Use the meaning and surrounding words to choose the form.
checks.correction: Į takes accusative: muziejų.

outcomes.goal: Use pas for visiting a person, including a named person.

models.title: The destination decides the preposition
pairs: I am going to the bank.
I am going to a male friend’s place.
I am going to a female friend’s place.
models.note: Use į for a place and pas for a person. Both need the destination form: draugas → draugą, draugė → draugę. The choice of į or pas depends on who or what you are going to.

models.title: Names change too
pairs: I am going to Tomas’s place.
I am going to Rasa’s place.
models.note: Tomas becomes Tomą, like draugas → draugą. Rasa becomes Rasą: -a changes to -ą. Keep pas because you are visiting a person.

checks.translation: On Friday I am going to a female friend’s place.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: After pas, use draugę.

checks.translation: On Monday I am going to Rasa’s place.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: After pas: Rasą.

outcomes.goal: Distinguish inside a building from beside it.

models.title: To the bank or by the bank?
pairs: I am going to the bank.
We are meeting by the bank.
We are meeting by the station.
models.note: Susitinkame means we are meeting. Prie (by) takes a different form: banko, stoties. Į names a destination; prie locates the meeting.

models.title: One place, three meanings
pairs: I am going to the café.
We are meeting by the café.
We are meeting in the café.
models.note: Į kavinę is a destination. Prie kavinės is beside the café. Kavinėje means in the café and needs no preposition. The endings carry a difference in meaning.

models.title: In the building
pairs: We are meeting in the bank.
We are meeting in the station.
We are meeting in the museum.
models.note: A location needs no į or prie. Compare bankas → banke, stotis → stotyje, muziejus → muziejuje. These say where you are, not where you are going.

checks.translation: We are meeting by the bank on Monday.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Prie takes banko, even when the place comes first.

checks.translation: We are meeting in the café on Monday.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Inside the café: kavinėje, without a preposition.

checks.translation: We are meeting by the café on Friday.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Prie takes kavinės.

checks.translation: We are meeting in the station on Friday.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: In the station: stotyje, without a preposition.

outcomes.goal: Follow a turn, locate it at a landmark, and give an endpoint.

models.title: Follow the direction
models.note: These are polite directions. Learn eikite (go) and pasukite (turn) as useful chunks here; you do not need to build other command forms yet.

models.title: At the bank or as far as the bank?
pairs: Go straight as far as the bank.
models.note: Prie tells you where the turn happens. Iki tells you how far to go. Both take banko; į banką would name a destination.

checks.translation: Turn left at the station.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Turn left: pasukite į kairę.

checks.translation: Turn left at the station.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: After prie: stoties.

checks.translation: Go straight as far as the station.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Iki identifies the endpoint: as far as the station.

outcomes.goal: Use the person form of eiti and važiuoti, including polite you.

models.title: I, you, we
pairs: I am going to the park.
You are going to the park.
We are going to the park.
models.note: The person changes the verb: aš einu, tu eini, mes einame. Į parką stays the same because the destination has not changed.

models.title: One form for she and he
pairs: She is going to the park.
He is going to the park.
models.note: Ji and jis both take eina. The verb changes with person, not with gender.

models.title: Asking politely
pairs: Where are you going? (polite or plural)
models.note: Tu takes eini. Jūs takes einate, whether you address one person politely or more than one person.

models.title: I, she, we
models.note: Compare važiuoju, važiuoja and važiuojame. Autobusu stays unchanged because the means of travel has not changed. Jis uses the same važiuoja as ji.

models.title: One person, two ways to address them
pairs: You travel by train. (polite or plural)
models.note: Tu takes važiuoji. Jūs takes važiuojate. Keep the same form in a question: Ar jūs važiuojate traukiniu?

checks.translation: You are going to the bank.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Tu takes eini; changing the place does not change the verb.

checks.translation: She is going to the museum.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Ji takes eina. A new destination does not change the person form.

checks.translation: Are you going to the café? (polite)
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Jūs takes einate, including when addressing one person politely.

checks.translation: We travel to Vilnius by train.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Mes takes važiuojame, whichever vehicle follows.

checks.translation: Do you travel by bus? (polite)
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Jūs takes važiuojate.

outcomes.goal: Give the day of a meeting using the when form.

models.title: When are we meeting?
models.note: For on Monday / on Friday, change -is to -į. Lithuanian does not need a separate word for on here.

checks.translation: On Friday I am going to the café.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: A day saying when takes -į.

checks.translation: On Friday I travel by train.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: The day tells when, so use penktadienį.

checks.translation: We are meeting on Friday evening.
checks.hint: Use the meaning and surrounding words to choose the form.
checks.correction: A day answering kada uses accusative: penktadienį.

outcomes.goal: Interpret full and half hours, including the next-hour convention.

models.title: At what time?
models.note: Use these time phrases to answer kelintą valandą? Both the number and valandą end in -ą. You will extend this pattern to the other hours later.

models.title: Halfway to the next hour
models.note: Pusę names the NEXT hour. Pusę trečios is halfway towards three: 2:30, not 3:30. Compare trečią for 3:00 with trečios after pusę.

checks.translation: We are meeting on Monday at two o’clock.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Antrą valandą — at two o’clock.

checks.translation: I am going to the café at 14:30.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: 14:30 is halfway to three: pusę trečios.

checks.translation: At 14:00 I am going to the museum.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: 14:00 is two o’clock: antrą valandą.

checks.translation: We are meeting at 5:30.
checks.hint: Use the meaning and surrounding words to choose the form.
checks.correction: Pusę names the next hour: pusę šeštos is 5:30.

outcomes.goal: Distinguish walking from vehicle travel and use the means-of-travel form.

models.title: By bus, by train, by taxi
models.note: Važiuoju is I travel by vehicle. By bus is autobusu; by train is traukiniu. Taksi stays unchanged. Compare the vehicle endings while the person stays the same.

models.title: The journey changes the verb
models.note: Use einu for going on foot and važiuoju for travelling by vehicle. Pėsčiomis makes on foot explicit.

models.title: Bus number two
models.note: When naming the bus, use antras autobusas. After važiuoju, both words describe the means of travel: antru autobusu, penktu autobusu.

checks.translation: I travel to the café by bus.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: The vehicle takes autobusu; the destination uses į kavinę.

checks.translation: I take bus number two to the museum.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: The means of travel uses antru autobusu.

checks.translation: I take bus number five to the station.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: The means of travel uses penktu autobusu.

checks.translation: I travel to Vilnius by train.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: By train: traukiniu.

checks.translation: We travel to the museum by bus.
checks.hint: Use the meaning and surrounding words to choose the form.
checks.correction: The means of transport uses instrumental: autobusu.

outcomes.goal: Distinguish often, rarely and never, and pair never with a negative verb.

models.title: Never needs a negative verb
pairs: I often go to the park.
I rarely go to the park.
I never go to the park.
models.note: Often and rarely keep the positive verb einu. With niekada (never), use neinu. Lithuanian uses both never and the negative verb.

models.title: The same pattern with transport
models.note: Add ne- to važiuoju after niekada: nevažiuoju.

checks.translation: I never go to the museum.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Niekada needs a negative verb: neinu.

checks.translation: I never travel by train.
checks.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
checks.correction: Use nevažiuoju after niekada, whichever vehicle follows.

outcomes.goal: Accept, decline, arrange and reschedule a meeting.

models.title: An invitation
pairs: Shall we go to the museum?
models.note: Einame…? can be an invitation. Mielai accepts it warmly; negaliu says you cannot. Learn the replies as useful phrases.

models.title: Place or day?
models.note: Kur asks for a place. Kada asks when. For an exact hour, ask kelintą valandą?

models.title: Keep the conversation going
models.note: A short alternative keeps the invitation open. Šiandien and rytoj do not change their endings. Evening is vakare.

outcomes.goal: Ask for a bus number, means of travel or walking route.

models.title: Three different questions
pairs: Which bus goes to the station?
How do you travel to the station?
How do I get to the station on foot?
models.note: Koks autobusas asks which bus. Kuo asks by what means; kaip can also ask how you travel. Kaip nueiti asks for a walking route.

applications.instruction: Choose the reply that answers the question.
applications.hint: Look at the part of the sentence that changes the meaning.
applications.correction: The question asks which bus: antras autobusas.

applications.instruction: Choose the reply that answers the question.
applications.hint: Look at the part of the sentence that changes the meaning.
applications.correction: Nueiti asks how to get there on foot. Eikite tiesiai gives a direction.

applications.translation: How do you travel to the station?
applications.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
applications.correction: Kuo asks by what means. Kaip is also natural here.

applications.translation: How do I get to the station on foot?
applications.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
applications.correction: Kaip nueiti — how to get there on foot.

applications.translation: Which bus goes to the station?
applications.hint: Check what the sentence needs to say. You can open the example for help.
applications.correction: Koks or kelintas asks which bus.

outcomes.goal: Understand an inspector and ask to top up a ticket.

models.title: Two sides of a ticket exchange
pairs: Please top up the electronic ticket.
models.note: At the kiosk, you ask to top up: papildyti. The inspector asks to see your ticket: parodyti. When handing it over or showing it, prašom can mean here you are.

applications.speaker: Kontrolierius
applications.instruction: You show your ticket. Say “Here you are.”
applications.hint: Your reply should mean: You show your ticket. Say “Here you are.”

applications.source: Please top up the electronic ticket.
applications.hint: Start with the action, then add the place or time.

outcomes.goal: Write a meeting message with a day, time, place and journey information.

applications.instruction: Write a meeting message. Give a day, time and place, then add how you travel or a short direction.
applications.sample: Susitinkame penktadienį, pusę šeštos prie muziejaus. Aš važiuoju autobusu. Prie stoties pasukite į kairę.
checklist: Give a day and time in their when forms.
Use prie + genitive for a meeting point.
Include one direction or means of transport.
applications.hint: Use short sentences and check each point in the list.
applications.correction: Compare your message with the example.
